What does carpet installation cost in Bothell, WA?

Most Bothell jobs come to $2,000–$4,500 start to finish. Add a staircase to a 1,200 sq ft main floor and you're usually looking at $5,500–$8,500. Per square foot, that's $4 to $7 installed, with nothing added later: carpet, pad and labor, new tack strip, the old floor hauled off. Grade swings the total more than anything — a rental near campus and a forever home at Thrashers Corner rarely want the same one — and you settle that at home, samples down on the floor.
Does the mobile carpet showroom come to Bothell?

Bothell sits on the county line — half King, half Snohomish — and we work both sides: Canyon Park cul-de-sacs, Thrashers Corner, the new townhomes downtown, student rentals near the university. The van shows up holding all three pad grades plus 20+ carpet samples, which go down on the actual floor being replaced. Then the measuring, then a written price handed to you on the spot. You pay nothing for the appointment.
What does carpet stretching cost in Bothell?

Against the cost of replacing the floor, a stretch runs about one-fifth — $99 per room to start in Bothell. The power stretcher pulls slack back out of a wavy upstairs hallway in a Canyon Park two-story and takes the trip spots down flat. If the fiber is still healthy and you can live with the color, that's the spend that makes sense.
What do carpeted stairs cost in Bothell?

Stair work starts at $18 per step, done waterfall or cap-and-band. Bothell's two-story stock from the 80s and 90s means we quote plenty of staircases — landings and pie-shaped winders go into the written number from the start, so nothing shows up as a surprise line later.
How long does a carpet install take in a Bothell home?

One day covers most Bothell homes. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a comfortable single day for the crew; a full house with heavy furniture or several flights can spill into a second. Your quote states the schedule in writing, so you know before install day rather than during it.
Will your installers move my furniture?

Yes. On most jobs the crew moves the big pieces — beds, couches, dressers, tables — and puts each one back once the carpet is in. Your part is the small stuff: closet floors, electronics, breakables and anything personal you'd rather carry yourself.
Should I stretch my Bothell carpet or replace it?

Three things decide it: the pile, the backing, and the smell. In the 90s two-stories around Canyon Park the ripples usually show up in an upstairs hall first — if the pile still comes back up there and the backing holds together, a $99-per-room stretch buys years. Replace when lanes are matted flat, seams have popped, the backing is powdering, or a professional cleaning left the pet odor behind. We make the call on site, before any quote.

What carpet holds up best with dogs and cats?

The pad matters as much as the fiber, especially in a rental near the UW Bothell campus that turns over every summer. A moisture-barrier pad — that upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot — catches a spill before it reaches the subfloor, where odor turns permanent. Over it, solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing: the color runs through the strand, so diluted bleach cleans it without fading anything.
What warranty comes with the installation?

Both pieces land in writing on your quote. The mill stands behind the carpet, generally 10 to 25 years against wear and stain, with the term set by grade. OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty covers the install itself — seams, stretch, transitions. And the pad underneath can decide whether that mill coverage holds, which is why all three pad grades come out of the van, in a campus rental or a Canyon Park two-story alike.
